overview.headline: Steady cruise speed sets flight distance and maximum range

keyPoints.point: Steady level flight keeps lift matched to weight and thrust matched to drag for constant speed
keyPoints.quote: an airplane can maintain a constant speed and level flight, in which the lift is equal to the weight

keyPoints.point: Steady wind keeps ground speed constant, letting distance flown increase with time aloft
keyPoints.quote: The ground speed remains constant as long as the wind speed is constant.

keyPoints.point: Maximum range equals ground speed multiplied by maximum time limited by fuel load
keyPoints.quote: The maximum distance that the aircraft can fly is then equal to the ground speed times the maximum time (tmax).

keyPoints.point: Military combat radius covers half the range for round trip missions needing return landing
keyPoints.quote: The combat radius would be half of the range as specified here.

keyTerms.gloss: constant speed relative to ground with steady wind
keyTerms.quote: The ground speed remains constant as long as the wind speed is constant.

keyTerms.gloss: forward force that balances drag in steady cruise
keyTerms.quote: in which the lift is equal to the weight, and the thrust is equal to the drag.

keyTerms.gloss: resisting force that slows airplane when thrust fades
keyTerms.quote: The drag then slows the airplane, which decreases the lift and, eventually, the airplane comes back to Earth.

keyTerms.gloss: upward force balancing weight in level flight
keyTerms.quote: an airplane can maintain a constant speed and level flight, in which the lift is equal to the weight

keyTerms.gloss: maximum distance aircraft can fly on fuel load
keyTerms.quote: We call this distance the maximum range (R) of the aircraft.
